# Jubilees Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Binding of Isaac (Aqedah); Mastema Defeated; Covenant Confirmed

---

**18:1** And it came to pass in the seventh week, in the first year thereof, in the first month in this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, that the word of the LORD came unto Abraham saying: "Abraham, Abraham"; and he said, "Here am I."

**18:2** And he said: "Take your son, your only son whom thou lovest — Isaac — and go into the high land, and offer him on one of the mountains which I will tell thee of."

**18:3** And he rose early in the morning and saddled his ass, and took two of his servants with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood of the burnt offering, and he arose and went to the place on the third day.

**18:4** And Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place afar off.

**18:5** And Abraham said unto his young men: "Abide ye here with the ass; and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you."

**18:6** And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife; and they went both of them together.

**18:7** And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said: "Father!" And he said: "Here am I, my son." And he said: "Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?"

**18:8** And Abraham said: "God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering, my son." So they went both of them together.

**18:9** And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.

**18:10** And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

**18:11** And I called unto him from heaven, and said unto him: "Abraham, Abraham." And he said: "Here am I."

**18:12** And I said unto him: "Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son, from me."

**18:13** And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.

**18:14** And Abraham called the name of that place "The LORD will provide": as it is said to this day, "In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen."

**18:15** And the angel of the LORD called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time, and said: "By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son:"

**18:16** "That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies."

**18:17** "And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice."

**18:18** And Abraham returned unto his young men; and they rose up and went together to Beersheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beersheba.

**18:19** And every year he came thither and built an altar on which he had built it at first; and he called on the name of the LORD, and said: "The LORD, the everlasting God."

**18:20** And he observed that festival with joy every year on this mountain — for seven days, eating and drinking and blessing the LORD God, the One who chose him and led him out from Ur of the Chaldees, and who established his covenant with him.

**18:21** And it came to pass that when the prince Mastema had seen all this, he was ashamed; and Abraham continued to be perfect in all his deeds before the LORD, and his name was honored before the LORD all the days of his life.

**18:22** For in all the temptations in which the LORD had tempted him, he was found faithful, and his soul loved God, and his soul clung to him; and he was not slow to act, and his soul was not impatient, because he loved God.

---
*EMET notes: The shift to first-person (vv.11-12) identifies the restraining angel as the angel-of-the-presence narrator throughout. Mastema's defeat and shame (v.21) is the climax of the Job-parallel: the accuser is proved wrong. The annual celebration on the mountain (vv.19-20) is Jubilees' etiology for a specific festival. V.20: "seven days" connects this to the later Passover/Unleavened Bread week (see ch.49).*
